state:
- The assay plan cites S1 for sorting “ROS-low versus oxidative ROS-high” fractions, but S1 defines ROS-low quiescent LSCs and S2 does not show that cytarabine-residual cells are ROS-high. Define the primary test population by S2 features (post-cytarabine residual cells with OXPHOS/FAO dependence) and keep ROS-low LSCs as a separate comparator arm.
- Bridge B treats ETC coupling of DHODH as evidence that the oxidative residual state is selectively dependent on de novo pyrimidine synthesis. A functional respiratory chain reoxidizes ubiquinone and can support DHODH, while pyrimidine dependence is set by salvage versus de novo synthesis, which neither S2 nor S4 measures. Pre-specify a head-to-head comparison of residual OXPHOS-high cells, bulk blasts, and ROS-low LSCs, and test whether ETC inhibition blunts rather than enhances the phenotype.
- The hypothesis is the most direct approved-drug reading of S4, and the validation is not decisive as written: DHODH overexpression is not feasible in the stated primary-specimen panel, AML genotype is unspecified, and falsifiers lack numeric cutoffs. Move the resistance allele to an engineered line, stratify a pre-specified differentiation-blocked subset, and lock thresholds for flux shift, CD11b/CD14 induction, limiting-dilution frequency, uridine rescue, and normal CD34+ sparing before calling the relationship confirmed or falsified.
